correctness.rationale: For every finite commutative ring, affine composition gives the additive homomorphism (v,e) -> (a-1)e-vb, whose image is exactly the ideal (a-1,b); the elementary finite-group kernel cardinality proves the centralizer formula. In a local ring the unit-ideal condition is equivalent to at least one unit among two parameters. In a chain ring the valuation filtration gives exactly the stated q-power multiplicities. If the local maximal ideal squares to zero, its residue-field vector-space rank partition gives the four complete multiplicities. Direct symbolic sums yield both commuting-probability formulas and the strictly positive q^3 comparison. A standalone Python program directly enumerated centralizers and generated ideals in twelve prime-field and integer-residue test cases and checked all formulas. No unproved all-q inference rests solely on those tests.

value.rationale: The all-element centralizer distribution is a natural invariant of the affine transformation semigroup and exactly reflects the two-generated ideal-size statistics of its coefficient ring. The theorem completely evaluates that invariant in two unrestricted structural families, including arbitrary chain length and radical-square-zero embedding dimension. Its universal leading atom contrasts with a provable strict commuting-probability difference for nonisomorphic rings having identical total and residue orders: q^3 versus q^3, for every prime power q. This gives a motivated first structural boundary beyond examples and is not just the uncounted elementary commutation equation.
